title: Compatible local embeddings of the two henselizations into a separable normalization
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a normal local domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, and $\Omega/K$ a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure]. Let $B\subset\Omega$ consist of the elements integral over $A$ (roots of monic polynomials over $A$), choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ with $\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak m$, and put $T=B_{\mathfrak q}$ and $E=T/\mathfrak m_T=B/\mathfrak q$. Let $H=A^{\mathrm h}$ be a henselization [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime], with residue field $\kappa$, and $R=A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ the compatible strict henselization [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] at a chosen separable closure $\kappa_s/\kappa$ [def-pd-separable-closure]. Then $B,T,H,R$ are normal domains, $\operatorname{Frac}(B)=\operatorname{Frac}(T)=\Omega$, $T$ is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and $E/\kappa$ is algebraic. The structural maps $A\to H\to R$ are injective local ind-etale maps [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], and $R/\mathfrak m_R=\kappa_s$. There exists a $\kappa$-embedding $j:\kappa_s\hookrightarrow E$. There is a unique local $A$-map $h:H\to T$; for every such $j$ there is a unique local $H$-map $i_j:R\to T$ inducing $j$. Both maps are injective. Thus each residue choice gives compatible embeddings $A\subseteq H\subseteq R\subseteq T\subseteq\Omega$; every compatible local embedding of $R$ into $T$ with that residue map equals $i_j$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-algebraic-extension-normal] to the algebraic extension $\Omega/K$. It makes $B$ a normal domain with fraction field $\Omega$. Since $\mathfrak q$ is maximal, hence prime, its complement contains no zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] to obtain the normal local domain $T=B_{\mathfrak q}\subset\Omega$ with fraction field $\Omega$. The residue identification $T/\mathfrak qT=B/\mathfrak q$ sends $(b/s)\bmod\mathfrak qT$ to $\bar b/\bar s$: every $s\notin\mathfrak q$ is already invertible in the field $B/\mathfrak q$. This also identifies the structural residue inclusion of $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$ with that induced by $A\subset B$ because $\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 0BSD, section-ramification, normalization and localization setup; algebra.tex Tags 0308 and 00GY.

proof.text: Every $e\in E=B/\mathfrak q$ has a representative $b\in B$ satisfying a monic equation over $A$. Reducing that equation modulo $\mathfrak q$ gives a monic (therefore nonzero) polynomial over $\kappa$ vanishing at $e$. Thus $E/\kappa$ is algebraic. For strict henselianity apply [lem-weil-pbc-gabber-quotient-localizations] with its normal domain equal to $B$, its ideal equal to $(0)$, and its prime equal to the image of $\mathfrak q$ in $B/(0)$. The fraction field is the separably closed field $\Omega$. The canonical identification $(B/(0))_{\mathfrak q/(0)}\simeq B_{\mathfrak q}=T$ transfers strict henselianity to $T$. In particular $T$ is henselian and $E$ is separably closed. This specialization supplies exactly the normal-local assertion of Tag 0BSQ without requiring the stronger assertion that $E$ is algebraically closed.

source.place: Tag 0BSQ, lemma-normal-local-domain-separablly-closed-fraction-field; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 09ZC, quotient-localization specialization with zero ideal.

proof.text: To justify the ind-etale structure for the specified ordinary henselization $H$, use [lem-trf-prime-pair-colimit-ind-etale-model] with prime $\mathfrak m$ of $A$. Since $A$ is local, $A_{\mathfrak m}\simeq A$ by $a/s\mapsto a s^{-1}$. This gives a henselian local ind-etale $A$-algebra $C$ with unchanged residue field. Apply [lem-trf-initial-henselian-colimit-comparison] to this $C$ and to the universal local henselian extension $H$ of [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. It gives an $A$-isomorphism $C\simeq H$ and transports the filtered etale presentation to the actual structural map $A\to H$. Consequently this map is local and ind-etale. The normal domain $A$ is a normal ring: each $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is a normal domain by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] (with $S=A\setminus\mathfrak p$, $0\notin S$). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain] to $A$ and the local colimit $H$: $H$ is a normal domain and $A\to H$ is injective.

source.place: Tags 0A02 and 0A03, lemma-henselization and lemma-henselization-local-ring; Tag 06DI, lemma-henselization-normal.

proof.text: Use [lem-wf-strict-henselization-finite-lifts] for $A$, its henselization $H$, and the chosen separable closure $\kappa_s/\kappa$. Its identification respects the $A$-structure and the canonical $H$-structure, so the given compatible strict henselization $R$ is the filtered colimit of the finite local etale $H$-algebras $B_e$ indexed by finite separable subextensions $e\subset\kappa_s$. Thus $H\to R$ is local and ind-etale, and $R$ is local with the specified residue field $\kappa_s$. By [lem-wf-finite-local-lift-colimit-structure], applied to this diagram (each $B_e/\mathfrak m_HB_e\simeq e$ is a field and $B_e$ is local, so $\mathfrak m_HB_e$ is its maximal ideal and the structure and transition maps are local), the colimit is strictly henselian; hence so is $R$. Therefore the induced local $A$-map $H\to R$ is the canonical one, the unique local $A$-map given by the universal property of $H$. Composition in [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] also gives that $A\to R$ is ind-etale. The normal domain $H$ is a normal ring by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] as in Step 3. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain] to $H$ and this local ind-etale $H$-algebra $R$ proves that $R$ is a normal domain and $H\to R$ is injective.

By Step 2, $E$ is separably closed. Since $\kappa_s/\kappa$ is separable algebraic, [lem-weil-pbc-separable-extension-embeds-separably-closed] gives a $\kappa$-algebra map $j:\kappa_s\to E$. A unital field map is injective. This works also when $A$ is a field: then $B=T=\Omega$ and $E=\Omega$ need only be separably closed.

source.place: Tag 0BSD, section-ramification, choice of residue embedding; the field case is separated in Tag 0BSQ.

proof.text: The inclusion $A\to T$ is local because $\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak m$. Since $T$ is henselian, [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime] gives the unique local $A$-map $h:H\to T$. Its residue map is the structural $\kappa\hookrightarrow E$, since the structural residue map $A\to H/\mathfrak m_H=\kappa$ is onto. Fix any $\kappa$-embedding $j:\kappa_s\hookrightarrow E$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] with base ring $H$, target $T$ endowed with $h$, ind-etale algebra $R$, prime $\mathfrak m_R$, and residue map $j$. The contracted prime in $H$ is $\mathfrak m_H$ for both $T$ and $R$, by locality, and the residue compatibility is exactly that $j$ is a $\kappa$-map. The conclusion gives a unique local $H$-map $i_j:R\to T$ inducing $j$. Any compatible local $A$-map $R\to T$ restricts on $H$ to $h$ by its uniqueness, hence is an $H$-map and equals $i_j$ if it induces $j$.

source.place: Tags 04GQ and 08HR, lemma-map-into-henselian-colimit; pione.tex Tag 0BSD, extension of the chosen residue embedding.

proof.text: Apply the final clause of [lem-dl-a1-ind-etale-domain-generic-field] first to the injective ind-etale domain map $A\to H$ and the unital map $H\xrightarrow{h}T\hookrightarrow\Omega$, and then to $A\to R$ and $R\xrightarrow{i_j}T\hookrightarrow\Omega$. The maps $A\to H$ and $A\to R$ are injective by Steps 3 and 4, and both composites restrict to the inclusion $A\hookrightarrow\Omega$. Thus both composites into the field $\Omega$ are injective, whence $h$ and $i_j$ are injective. As $i_j$ is an $H$-map, its restriction to $H$ is $h$. These maps therefore realize $A\subseteq H\subseteq R\subseteq T\subseteq\Omega$, with the uniqueness for the chosen residue map already established in Step 6.
